A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same PCR research work, including Appendices A–B. Their methods, experiments, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original vehicle, pedestrian and multiclass detection evaluation results, together with ablations, robustness experiments and correlation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised quantitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: PCR retains the merged-box consistency measure, confidence-weighted reliability measure and linear regression procedure in Section 3. Combining PCR with BoS and using piecewise regression were already explored in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same vehicle, pedestrian and multiclass datasets, augmentation- and corruption-based meta-datasets, corruption severities and low-mAP test scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: PS, ES, AC, ATC and BoS remain the main comparators. The BoS comparisons in multiclass and piecewise-regression experiments and the PCR-plus-BoS comparison also retain their membership.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 changes the reported defaults from c=0.5, alpha=0.2, k_C=-60 and k_R=10 to 0.4, 0.1, -10 and 20, and Figure B.2 revises the scale-parameter grids. Section 5.1 still lists the original defaults, leaving the actual configuration ambiguous. The broader evaluation design is unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure B.2 revises the hyperparameter sensitivity investigation: the k_C sweep shifts toward values near zero, and the k_R sweep extends to 40 instead of 20. The existing component ablations, severity tests, set-size analyses and piecewise-regression investigation remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging BoS over three runs and use the same correlation reporting practices. Neither introduces additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The core quantitative evidence is substantially revised across main and appendix experiments. PCR's average RMSE changes from 5.03 to 4.61 in Table 1, 3.60 to 3.57 in Table 2, and 7.58 to 7.75 in Table B.1; individual shifts include 5.47 to 3.82 for augmentation-based vehicle evaluation with RetinaNet/Swin. Ablation results, correlations and some baseline results in Table B.15 also change. Conflicting tuning descriptions prevent interpreting these as controlled, same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the definitions of consistency and reliability, and the regression formulations are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: PCR for estimating detection performance without target annotations, the corruption-based meta-dataset and improved estimation accuracy. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The confidence/localization explanation, component-complementarity arguments and robustness interpretations remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 retains the same qualification about nonlinear relationships and separate regression in the low-mAP regime.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies that each hyperparameter analysis uses the scores affected by that hyperparameter and revises the documented defaults. Its disagreement with Section 5.1 creates a reproducibility ambiguity. Appendix A's training, hardware and software details and the code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against BoS and other prior approaches, and references [1]–[48] are unchanged.

P1.justification: Prose edits are limited, principally Appendix B.2's clarification of the hyperparameter analyses and its added reference to Tables 1–2. Section organization and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 adds a dataset and marker legend and adjusts panel placement. Several plots revise axes and annotation placement; Figures B.4–B.5 use thicker black regression lines. The figure/table inventory and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Clearer plot legends and the tuning clarification provide limited benefits, but v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies. Appendix B.2's defaults now contradict Section 5.1, while Sections 5.2–5.3 retain averages of 5.03 and 3.60 despite Tables 1–2 reporting 4.61 and 3.57. The consistency-only ablation also differs between Table 3 and Tables 4–5. These discrepancies reduce reproducibility and confidence in the reporting, outweighing the presentation gains.
